purpose: W11-A: define and prove exact-release REG.RU backup/PITR/restore/disaster-recovery acceptance with owner-approved RPO/RTO targets and immutable evidence, without using CI-only restore as production proof or mutating production during governance.
authorization: Owner instruction on 2026-09-05 to continue PC-CROP and keep production only on REG.RU. This staged governance branch performs no production mutation. Exact runtime drills require the later accepted operations procedure and safe isolated restore target.
requiredInvariants: CI/local restore rehearsals are engineering evidence only and never counted as production backup/PITR/DR proof.
RPO and RTO targets are explicit approved policy values before terminal acceptance. The staged scope does not invent or silently select business recovery objectives.

Every production backup evidence record binds REG.RU environment identity, PostgreSQL instance/database identity, exact release SHA/schema migration head, backup method/type, start/end time, size/checksum/encryption metadata, retention class and result.
PITR evidence proves the required WAL/log/archive chain exists and that an isolated restore can target a timestamp between full/base backups according to the accepted RPO policy.
Restore rehearsal always uses an isolated non-production restore target or explicitly safe replacement procedure; it never overwrites the live production database during an acceptance test.

Restored database acceptance verifies schema/migration head, critical row counts/checksums, RLS/roles/policies, audit/outbox chains, representative Deal/Inventory/Settlement/Document authorities and application read-only smoke against the exact release.
Restore credentials/secrets are never committed to the repository or evidence artifact; evidence stores references/fingerprints and redacted command metadata only.

DR procedure defines loss/corruption/unavailable-host scenarios, detection/decision authority, backup selection, restore, application cutover, DNS/network implications, verification, rollback and incident evidence.
A successful backup command without a proven restore is not BACKUP/DR terminal PASS. A successful restore without exact data/security/application verification is not DR PASS.
Recovery timing is measured from declared incident/start markers to validated service/readiness completion, not from a synthetic script subsection.
Failure, timeout, checksum mismatch, missing WAL, schema mismatch, RLS drift or application-readiness failure causes acceptance FAIL_CLOSED and preserves all evidence.
No Netlify/Vercel/alternate production topology is introduced. Production acceptance is REG.RU only.
Registration, Role Eligibility, Federal Accounting lock #4321, business data/authority schemas and mandatory recurring cost remain unchanged by the governance/runbook slice.
acceptance: Policy verification fails until explicit RPO/RTO targets are approved and recorded; no placeholder target can produce PASS.
A real REG.RU backup produces immutable evidence with exact release/schema/checksum and passes independent artifact verification.
An isolated full/base restore and a PITR restore each pass schema/RLS/authority/data/readiness verification against their expected recovery points.
A deliberately corrupted/wrong backup, missing archive segment or wrong migration head is detected and rejected.
Measured recovery-point loss and recovery time satisfy the approved RPO/RTO targets for the accepted drill; otherwise the criterion remains FAIL.
DR drill evidence includes exact operator actions/timestamps, incident scenario, selected backup/recovery point, verification results and rollback/cutover outcome.
No production data is destroyed/overwritten by the rehearsal and no credential/secret is persisted in GitHub artifacts.
Exact-head review plus production REG.RU evidence are required before any DR criterion receives terminal PASS.
remainingTerminalBoundary: Actual RPO/RTO target values require explicit owner/business approval; this governance scope deliberately does not fabricate them.
Real REG.RU backup/PITR features and access must exist and be exercised; repository scripts cannot substitute for provider/runtime evidence.
Periodic recurring DR drill cadence and alerting remain operations policy after first terminal acceptance.
Any destructive production recovery action outside an isolated rehearsal requires incident/change authorization appropriate to production operations.
